scope: Isolated authenticated Chromium executor with an actual Hub SQL task, assignment, ownership lease and pre-reserved Hub Registry test run
verified: Hub Registry issues SRC/RUN identities before Chromium starts; browser receives only the closed assigned projection
Actual current Task/project, Worker assignment and fenced ownership lease are checked under SQL locks before result completion
Changed input, foreign assignment/worker/project, stale lease, cancelled Task and modified evidence identity are denied
Browser completion follows Hub checks of actual Native tasks and pause/resume/cancel/retry events
Identical result replay verifies the original completed result; changed or unverified outcomes cannot be promoted
Synthetic test scope cannot satisfy a production release gate
Host source snapshot includes mounted frontend source/config and rejects changes during the gate
The cached browser image is resolved and pinned to its immutable Docker image ID

solid_review.protected: Browser coordination delegates Registry/SQL admission to a dedicated Hub adapter; host source/image binding is separated from the runner loop (SRP/DIP). Worker receives a closed projection without identity issuance authority.
solid_review.preserved_debt: SyntheticBrowserEvidence composes task/assignment/lease persistence and result validation for this bounded fixture. The existing browser coordination/public API fixtures remain coupled to SQL/Flask composition.

limits: The dedicated bootstrap token admits this synthetic acceptance executor only; it is not productive registered-Worker admission
The reserved browser run covers Chromium execution, not earlier bundle preparation or every independent core component test
Productive provider/image rollout and release acceptance remain separate requirements
